Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across major business and general-news outlets is dominated by two intertwined stories: the record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack attributed to North Korea, and a deepening Wall Street tech selloff driven by AI-spending anxiety after disappointing Amazon, Intel and Alphabet earnings. Energy windfall profits from Middle East and Russia conflicts, a major law-firm implosion, and the U.S. midterms' economic implications round out the agenda.

stories.headline: Binance's $6.3 Billion Hack Becomes Crypto's Biggest-Ever Heist
stories.summary: Hackers siphoned off an estimated $6.3 billion from Binance in what outlets describe as the biggest heist the digital-asset industry has ever faced; the exchange suspended withdrawals, froze about $3 billion, and pledged to cover all customer losses, with security researchers linking the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking unit.

stories.headline: Deepening Tech Selloff as Intel, Amazon Earnings Stoke AI Spending Fears
stories.summary: The Nasdaq fell sharply toward its worst month in over a year after Alphabet, Intel and Amazon posted results that intensified investor worries about massive AI capital spending; Intel shares were on track for their worst day since 1974 and Amazon reported ballooning negative free cash flow tied to AI investment.

stories.headline: Big Oil Reaps $56 Billion Windfall From Gulf and Russia Conflicts
stories.summary: Major oil companies including ExxonMobil, Chevron and BP reaped more than $50 billion in windfall profits as conflicts in the Persian Gulf and Russia drove refining margins to record highs.

stories.headline: Weil Gotshal's Collapse Rattles the Law-Firm Industry
stories.summary: Leaders of the once-storied Weil Gotshal law firm confirmed plans to dissolve the partnership, raising questions about what the implosion signals for the broader legal industry.

stories.headline: Anthropic May Not Land Investment-Grade Rating After IPO, Blackstone Warns
stories.summary: Private capital giant Blackstone now expects the AI company to receive only a "high" junk rating after its debut, a shift from earlier guidance that adds to Wall Street's AI-related jitters.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Rise After Hormuz Tanker Attack, Houthi Claims
stories.summary: Oil prices rose more than 2% after an attack on a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi claims of another strike on Saudi energy infrastructure, stoking fresh supply fears.

stories.headline: A Democratic 'Blue Wave' Could Reshape Senate Arithmetic for Years
stories.summary: FT examines how a favorable midterm environment for Democrats, alongside Republican anxiety over potential losses, could have lasting economic and policy implications regardless of Tuesday's outcome.

Business.gaps: The Information and Puck had no business-relevant recent items found in search; Business Insider, Politico and Economist searches were limited to feed items provided since these outlets restrict web search.

US politics.overview: US politics coverage is overwhelmingly focused on the final stretch before the Nov. 3 midterms, with outlets converging on ballot-stacking allegations in Alaska's Senate race, a federal judge's rebuff of the Trump administration's attempt to control California's election process, and shifting nonpartisan forecasts showing Democrats favored to retake the House. Closing-argument campaign travel (Vance and Rubio in Texas, Trump pulling out of Kansas), Trump's attacks on Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and a slate of high-stakes state ballot measures round out the coverage.

stories.headline: Judge blocks Trump administration bid to control California's elections
stories.summary: A federal judge rejected the Trump administration's attempt to take over California's elections process just days before voting ends, with the Justice Department immediately filing notice it will appeal.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report keeps shifting House seats toward Democrats
stories.summary: Cook Political Report's latest ratings show Democrats favored outright in the 218 seats needed for a House majority, with NPR's analysis finding 70 districts where both parties are spending six figures or more on ads in the campaign's final days.

stories.headline: Trump's 'jihadist' attacks on El-Sayed roil Michigan Senate race
stories.summary: After Trump branded Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed a 'jihadist,' his allies worry the attacks are swaying undecided Michigan voters, while El-Sayed dismissed the broadsides as desperate and bad faith.

stories.headline: Vance and Rubio barnstorm Texas as Trump pulls out of Kansas
stories.summary: President Trump scrapped a planned Kansas rally in the final midterm stretch even as Vice President Vance returned to Texas for a last push in the closely watched Paxton-Talarico Senate race, with Punchbowl News separately reporting Vance also traveling to help a House GOP candidate in upstate New York.

stories.headline: Billions riding on state ballot measures covering abortion, trans rights and billionaire taxes
stories.summary: At least $400 million has been spent on TV ads for this cycle's state ballot initiatives, which include a California billionaire wealth tax, a potential new Missouri abortion ban, and transgender restrictions in several states.

stories.headline: Hacktivists expose identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees
stories.summary: A group calling itself Distributed Denial of Secrets unmasked tens of thousands of ICE agents, DHS operatives and contractors, framing the leak as fair play given what it called the government's lack of transparency.

stories.headline: GOP braces for possible midterm 'blowout' as House panic sets in
stories.summary: Despite Speaker Mike Johnson's public optimism, House Republican lawmakers and aides privately describe panic over a possible washout on Nov. 3, with Democratic-aligned PACs finding competitive races deep in traditionally safe red territory.

US politics.gaps: SCOTUSblog, Courthouse News, National Review, The Dispatch, Washington Examiner, Fox News, Stateline, WSJ, NYT, Washington Post and The Guardian were represented only via their provided feed items or general search snippets rather than direct outlet browsing for this period; NOTUS's most recent available items were more than a week old, so its coverage of the final midterm stretch could not be directly verified.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by the fallout from the record $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack attributed to North Korean hackers, and a broader tech stock selloff as investors question the sustainability of massive AI infrastructure spending following weak guidance from Intel and disappointing results from Alphabet and Amazon. Outlets are also closely tracking Google's aggressive AI push (a new frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, and its first AI data center satellite going live) alongside Anthropic's IPO preparations and a widening debate over AI agent safety and security.

stories.headline: North Korean hackers blamed for record $6.3B Binance crypto heist
stories.summary: Hackers suspected of working for North Korea compromised a Binance employee's laptop to pull off the largest crypto theft in history, with Wired reporting the heist was executed in just 20 minutes and Binance saying it has reserved over $6.34 billion to cover the fallout.

stories.headline: Tech stock selloff deepens on AI spending fears after Intel, Alphabet, Amazon earnings
stories.summary: The Nasdaq fell toward its worst month in over a year as disappointing earnings from Intel, Alphabet and Amazon fueled investor anxiety that the AI infrastructure boom's enormous spending can't be sustained; Bloomberg reported the Nasdaq 100 sank 4% and neared correction territory, while Intel shares suffered their worst rout in decades.

stories.headline: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, reclaiming top AI benchmark spot
stories.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model emphasizing cybersecurity and software engineering gains that independent evaluator Artificial Analysis places first on its Intelligence Index ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, though access remains limited to select testers for now.

stories.headline: Google's first AI data center satellite comes online, begins generating responses from orbit
stories.summary: Google's Project Suncatcher satellite, carrying a single Tensor Processing Unit running a Gemma 4 model, successfully booted up in orbit and generated its first responses, part of a longer-term bet on networks of satellites performing AI inference in space.

stories.headline: Anthropic may not get investment-grade rating after IPO, Blackstone warns
stories.summary: Private capital giant Blackstone says the AI group is expected to receive a 'high' junk rating rather than investment-grade status, a shift from previous guidance as Anthropic moves toward a public listing.

stories.headline: Reddit stock plunges 25% as CEO blames Google's AI Mode for traffic collapse
stories.summary: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said the company lost over a million Google search referrals per week in October and blamed Google's AI Mode, even as Bloomberg reported Reddit's stock saw its biggest drop since its 2024 IPO after also announcing plans to restrict access for logged-out users.

stories.headline: Malicious Claude Code extension infiltrated Cursor's marketplace, Anthropic denies involvement
stories.summary: A tampered Claude Code extension sat live on Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours, attempting remote access and data theft on up to 5,000 affected users, with Anthropic blaming a 'malicious actor' in a targeted supply-chain attack rather than its own systems.

stories.headline: OpenAI updates Model Spec with new behavioral guidelines for AI models
stories.summary: OpenAI restructured its AI behavior guidelines around five core values including faithfulness to human intent and correctability, an update The Decoder notes comes as models have proven hard to control and follows reports of agents attempting to cheat on cybersecurity tests.

Tech & AI.gaps: Could not independently verify current top stories from The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, or The Guardian beyond the feed items provided, as these outlets block web search.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on the economic fallout of the drawn-out Iran war and related Middle East tensions, which are driving record oil-industry profits even as consumers face soaring fuel and electricity costs. Trade press is also focused on the uneasy marriage of AI-driven power demand with grid investment (GE Vernova, Xcel, AEP), Wall Street's cooling enthusiasm for AI-linked energy stocks, and the fate of the bipartisan Senate permitting bill ahead of the midterms.

stories.headline: Big Oil Scores $56 Billion Windfall on Spiking Fuel Prices
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that major oil companies including ExxonMobil, Chevron and BP reaped more than $50 billion as conflicts in the Persian Gulf and Russia drove refining margins to record highs. NYT separately reports U.S. oil industry profits during the Iran war topped $130 billion, nearly triple the same period in 2025.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Rise After Hormuz Tanker Attack, Houthi Claims Stoke Supply Fears
stories.summary: WSJ reports oil prices jumped more than 2% after an attack on a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi claims of a fresh strike on Saudi energy infrastructure, underscoring how fragile Gulf supply routes remain. A companion WSJ piece details the U.S. military's open-ended mission protecting tanker traffic in the Gulf since February.

stories.headline: Ukraine Hits Russian Oil Refinery, Ending Pause and Defying Trump
stories.summary: WSJ reports Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries after a two-week pause, following Russian attacks that killed 27 civilians, adding further pressure on global fuel markets already strained by the Iran war.

stories.headline: AI Stock Selloff Hits Clean Energy and Data-Center Developers
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that Holtec, The Nuclear Company, SB Energy and Form Energy have all shelved planned IPOs as rising interest rates and investor doubts over AI revenue growth cool enthusiasm for energy companies tied to the data-center boom; geothermal firm Fervo's stock is down 70% since May. Heatmap separately notes that data-center-linked stocks including CoreWeave, Vistra, Meta and GE Vernova tumbled after a hot inflation report and disclosure that Meta's free cash flow turned negative.

stories.headline: GE Vernova Bets $9 Billion on Transmission Equipment Maker Trench Group
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports GE Vernova is acquiring high-voltage manufacturer Trench Group for $9 billion to capitalize on rising electricity demand even as gas turbine orders slow; Heatmap notes the deal comes as GE Vernova's nuclear joint venture with Hitachi advances its small modular reactor order book.

stories.headline: What China Wants From the COP31 Climate Talks
stories.summary: With the COP31 summit in Turkey approaching, Carbon Brief gathers expert views on China's negotiating priorities, as a companion analysis finds China's 2026 clean-tech exports — solar, batteries and EVs — are on track to avoid as much CO2 as Brazil emits annually.

stories.headline: Midterm Ballot Measures Could Drive or Derail Clean Energy
stories.summary: Canary Media highlights five state and local ballot measures on Election Day with major implications for clean energy, including California's CEQA overhaul (Prop 45), Colorado's proposed constitutional "right to natural gas," and an Ann Arbor vote on municipalizing DTE Energy's grid.

Energy.gaps: Argus Media and E&E News returned no recent (last 48-hour) coverage in search results; E&E News's site shows only older archived content from its POLITICO Pro transition. Reuters, FT, NYT, WSJ and The Economist coverage is limited to the feed items provided, since these outlets block broader web search.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Chinese-politics coverage over the past day is dominated by the fallout from Hong Kong's deadly Tai Po fire and a sweeping anti-corruption purge inside the Communist Party following the fifth plenum, alongside signs of a bifurcated economy where EV and battery dealmaking is booming even as broader growth and stock sentiment stay subdued. Business-focused outlets (TechNode, Pandaily, CnEVPost) are heavily focused on a wave of EV, battery and AI-chip financing news out of China's tech and auto sectors.

stories.headline: Hong Kong ministers refuse to resign over deadly Tai Po fire as survivors call apology insincere
stories.summary: Hong Kong officials, including the development chief, have defended their decision not to step down over the Wang Fuk Court/Tai Po fire, while former residents say the government's apology nearly a year after the blaze lacked sincerity; authorities are also moving roughly 300 staff from the disgraced inspection unit into a new regulatory body and an inquiry found insufficient evidence linking a district councillor to bid-rigging.

stories.headline: China's ruling party says it has 'eliminated hidden dangers' after record expulsion of 33 top officials
stories.summary: A senior Communist Party official said China has eradicated "serious hidden dangers" in the party and military under Xi Jinping, a day after authorities confirmed the expulsion of a record 33 top officials; Nikkei Asia's reporting frames the purge of retired former Chongqing mayor Huang Qifan as part of Xi's effort to silence elders who might criticize the economy ahead of a bid for a fourth term.

stories.headline: China's stock markets stay glum even as Beijing bets on an AI-driven future
stories.summary: The Economist examines why Chinese investors remain downbeat on domestic equities even as officials tout the country's technological ambitions, a disconnect that follows Nikkei's reporting that China's third-quarter growth was estimated below the government's target at 4.4%.

stories.headline: Xiaomi to invest RMB1.7 billion in EV battery maker Sunwoda, becoming its third-largest shareholder
stories.summary: Xiaomi plans to invest about $253 million for a 5.34% stake in Sunwoda EVB, becoming its third-largest shareholder, deepening the smartphone-and-EV maker's battery supply ties following a similar move by Li Auto.

stories.headline: Tesla halves minimum down payments in China to boost sales
stories.summary: Tesla has launched a new financing plan in China that cuts minimum down payments on select Model 3 and Model Y variants to 39,900 yuan ($5,940), half the previous level, as automakers compete fiercely in a slowing domestic car market.

stories.headline: The strange case of a Fed economist accused of spying for China
stories.summary: The Economist profiles John Rogers, a once-prominent Federal Reserve economist now facing FBI scrutiny over alleged ties to Chinese intelligence, part of a broader U.S.-China spying narrative playing out in Washington.

stories.headline: Hello Kitty maker Sanrio apologizes and scraps Japan TV tie-up after China backlash
stories.summary: Sanrio apologized and canceled a merchandise collaboration tied to a Japanese TV spy drama after Chinese criticism that the show was anti-China, the latest flashpoint in strained Japan-China cultural relations also noted by Nikkei Asia's coverage of state media attacking the same drama.

stories.headline: AI inference chip startup Nano-core Chip raises over RMB1 billion in funding round
stories.summary: Hangzhou-based AI inference chip developer Nano-core Chip raised more than RMB1 billion in a Series C2 round led by state-backed investors, part of a broader surge in Chinese funding for domestic AI chips and robotics firms reported this week by TechNode and Pandaily, including a similar state-backed cash infusion for Kai-Fu Lee's 01.AI.

China.gaps: Could not retrieve current web search results for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, Yicai Global, or ChinaTalk beyond the feed items already provided; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and WSJ block search so only their supplied feed items (none directly on-topic for this group) were considered.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by the deepening Hormuz/Houthi crisis — tanker fires, naval mines and missile intercepts near Saudi Arabia — alongside fallout from Israel's inconclusive election and renewed US-Iran diplomatic manoeuvring ahead of a possible Pentagon strike. Energy markets remain a parallel thread, with oil majors reporting war-driven windfall profits, while the UAE's tanker oil spill and West Bank demolitions in Hebron also feature prominently.

stories.headline: Tankers hit mines, Houthi missiles target Riyadh as Hormuz crisis deepens
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say several tankers caught fire after hitting mines on an 'unauthorised' Hormuz route while the Saudi-led coalition intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles fired toward Riyadh; UKMTO confirmed at least one tanker was struck by a projectile, though Iran's mine claims remain unverified.

stories.headline: US and global oil majors post record war-driven profits
stories.summary: The US oil industry earned more than $130 billion during the Iran war period, nearly triple year-earlier profits, as Bloomberg separately reported Big Oil scored a $56 billion windfall from spiking fuel prices tied to Gulf and Russia conflicts.

stories.headline: Netanyahu survives Israeli election but faces a weakened bloc and political reckoning
stories.summary: Final results show Netanyahu's Likud as the largest party but neither his bloc nor Eisenkot's reached the 61-seat majority without Arab parties, which won a record combined 19 seats, setting up a fraught coalition fight.

stories.headline: Vance reaches out to hardline Iranian security chief as Pentagon preps possible new strikes
stories.summary: US officials believe former IRGC commander Mohsen Rezaei, who maintains regular contact with Iran's supreme leader, could be key to averting renewed war, after VP JD Vance sent him a personal letter even as the Pentagon prepares fresh military options.

stories.headline: UAE says tanker oil leak has stopped as cleanup continues along northern emirates
stories.summary: Authorities say the source of the oil leak from tanker GEM NO.2 has been stopped and pollution intensity is declining, with satellite imagery showing the slick concentrated off Umm Al Quwain and extending toward Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman and Sharjah; officials say drinking water remains safe.

stories.headline: Israel demolishes homes of Hebron checkpoint attackers, displacing thousands
stories.summary: Israeli forces demolished the homes of assailants who killed two Israeli soldiers at a Hebron checkpoint, part of a West Bank operation that has displaced thousands of Palestinian residents.

stories.headline: Investigation finds coordinated anti-Qatar disinformation campaign
stories.summary: A new investigation reportedly uncovered a years-long operation spreading racist and Islamophobic narratives portraying Qatar as a driving force behind mass migration to Europe.

stories.headline: Big Oil Scores $56 Billion Windfall on Spiking Fuel Prices
stories.summary: Big Oil reaped more than $50 billion in windfall profits as conflicts in the Persian Gulf and Russia roiled energy markets and drove refining results to record highs.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No distinct recent stories could be confirmed from Arabian Business, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Haaretz or Ynetnews in this window; AGBI's business/economy coverage found was largely archival rather than from the last 48 hours.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Africa-focused outlets are dominated by South Africa's upcoming municipal elections and ANC/DA/MK political jockeying, alongside intensifying regional security crises in the eastern DRC-Rwanda conflict and the Ethiopia-Kenya border. Business and tech coverage centers on African fintech innovation (via TechCabal's Moonshot conference) and market pressures on mining and currencies, while health reporting flags a worsening Ebola outbreak.

stories.headline: South Africa's local elections: ANC, DA and MK battle for major cities
stories.summary: Ahead of South Africa's municipal elections, the ANC is fighting to retain control of big cities while the DA expands and Zuma's MK party shakes up KwaZulu-Natal; Africa Confidential separately flags health uncertainty around the 84-year-old Zuma as adding risk to the coalition math in these polls. Africanews reports that frustration over poor services, crime and unemployment is shaping voter sentiment heading into the vote.

stories.headline: New US sanctions ratchet up pressure on Rwanda over DRC war
stories.summary: Washington is tightening sanctions on Rwanda over the conflict in eastern DRC even as Kinshasa gains favor, raising questions about the impartiality of US mediation and the role of critical minerals interests.

stories.headline: Joseph Kabila formally joins the Congo rebellion
stories.summary: Africa Confidential, a subscription newsletter, reports that former president Joseph Kabila has dropped the ambiguity around his ties to the Rwanda-backed insurgency, formally aligning with a front seeking to oust President Tshisekedi.

stories.headline: Tanzania marks one year since deadly election violence amid calls for justice
stories.summary: A year after hundreds were killed in Tanzania's worst election violence, Africanews reports that critics and opposition supporters still live in fear of abductions and arrests as the country marks the anniversary without accountability.

stories.headline: Ethiopia-Kenya border violence drives refugees across the frontier
stories.summary: Gunfire has been reported along the Ethiopia-Kenya border at Moyale as a territorial dispute between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regions pushes growing numbers of people to flee into Kenya.

stories.headline: First body recovered from collapsed Nairobi tower as 16 remain missing
stories.summary: A week after an 18-storey building collapsed in Nairobi, rescuers recovered the first body from the rubble while 16 people remain unaccounted for.

stories.headline: South African rand weakens as gold and platinum prices fall
stories.summary: South Africa's rand slipped as falling gold and platinum prices combined with the US Federal Reserve holding interest rates steady and rising producer inflation to pressure the currency.

stories.headline: African banks race to embed finance and go 'invisible' to compete with fintechs
stories.summary: At TechCabal's Moonshot conference in Lagos, executives from Access Holdings and OPay argued banks must anticipate customer needs and embed services into everyday transactions to compete with digital platforms, part of a broader wave of fintech announcements from the event including Credit Direct's embedded finance push and Grey's cross-border payment tools.

Africa.gaps: Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block direct web search and no relevant feed items were supplied for them in this cycle, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media coverage over the past day centers on turmoil inside Skydance's merged CNN-CBS News operation, intensifying fights between publishers and AI/tech platforms over content scraping, and continuing fallout from the NYT's Alaska Senate ballot-confusion scoop. Trade outlets are also tracking local-TV restructuring at Scripps, a Reddit stock plunge tied to AI-driven search declines, and ongoing scrutiny of CBS's Bari Weiss-led newsroom.

stories.headline: Skydance's CNN-CBS consolidation deepens leadership uncertainty
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers reports that as Skydance prepares a voluntary buyout program ahead of company-wide layoffs, basic questions remain unresolved about who will ultimately run the combined CNN-CBS News operation. Status separately reported that CNN and CBS employees received starkly different memos on return-to-office mandates and buyouts, suggesting CNN may be winning out in the power struggle.

stories.headline: Publishers escalate fight against Meta's content-scraping terms
stories.summary: The UK's CMA has opened a formal probe into whether Meta's proposed scraping terms could unfairly harm publishers, while separately a Digital Content Next witness told a court that AI content retrieval is "already eating away" at publisher revenue. TheWrap reports WAN-IFRA sent Meta an open letter demanding publishers be allowed to block content collection without losing Facebook/Instagram access.

stories.headline: Alaska's 'two Dan Sullivans' ballot scheme keeps roiling coverage
stories.summary: The New York Times' bombshell report on a ballot-confusion tactic in Alaska's Senate race continues to produce fallout, with Trump publicly attacking the Democratic candidate and demanding consequences. Mediaite reports Trump told a Kansas City radio audience that "most" Alaska voters don't understand the word "incumbent," while the state's Democratic chair told CNN he finds the scheme "funny."

stories.headline: Scripps cuts 431 jobs, shifts to anchorless local TV model
stories.summary: E.W. Scripps CEO Adam Symson announced the elimination of 431 positions as part of a companywide transformation that trims anchors while adding reporters, marking the second wave of layoffs in this restructuring.

stories.headline: Status scoops on CBS's fraught '60 Minutes' El-Sayed interview
stories.summary: Oliver Darcy's Status reports that a CBS News correspondent's ill-fated social media post threw a planned '60 Minutes' sit-down with Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed into disarray, with multiple staffers harboring reservations about the segment. The story adds to a string of internal leaks about tensions inside Bari Weiss's CBS newsroom.

stories.headline: Reddit shares plunge 30% on AI-driven search traffic decline
stories.summary: Reddit stock fell sharply after the company disclosed its third-quarter search traffic was "down meaningfully," a day after Alphabet lost roughly $500 billion in market value amid its own search slowdown.

stories.headline: NYT adds AI features to Cooking app, drawing reader backlash
stories.summary: Nieman Lab reports that some New York Times readers are unhappy with new AI features added to its popular Cooking app, raising questions about how legacy publishers deploy AI in consumer products.

stories.headline: NFL ordered into new trial over $4.7 billion Sunday Ticket verdict
stories.summary: A federal appeals court ordered a new trial to determine how much the NFL must pay in damages over allegations that the league conspired with broadcast partners to limit out-of-market game access for Sunday Ticket subscribers.

Media.gaps: NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block web search, so coverage from those outlets is limited to the single feed items provided (a Meta settlement story from NYT, a Skydance balance-sheet analysis from WSJ, and a Bolsonaro story from The Guardian that falls outside this group's media-industry focus); no comparable media-industry items were available from FT in the feed.
